stem: The neuron's sodium-potassium pump is best described as:

choices.text: A passive channel that lets ions flow along their gradients
An active transport mechanism that moves sodium out and potassium in
A receptor site that binds neurotransmitters on the dendrites
The fatty sheath that insulates axons and speeds conduction

explanation: The sodium-potassium pump actively (using ATP) exports 3 Na+ and imports 2 K+ per cycle to maintain the resting potential. Myelin (D) insulates axons; ion channels (A) are passive.

stem: A researcher damages a rat's cerebellum. Which behavior is most likely to be impaired?
explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movement and balance. Hypothalamus (B) regulates hunger; hippocampus (C) consolidates new memories.

stem: Split-brain patients can best identify an object placed in their left visual field by:

choices.text: Pointing to it with their left hand
Writing its name with their right hand
Describing it verbally with both eyes closed

explanation: Left-visual-field information goes to the right hemisphere, which controls the left hand but (after corpus callosum severing) cannot feed the language-dominant left hemisphere.

stem: In a study, children who saw an adult punished for hitting a doll later hit the doll less, but when offered rewards for imitating, they performed the behavior as often as other children. This demonstrates:

choices.text: Observational learning with latent, unreinforced acquisition
Classical conditioning of aggressive emotional responses
Spontaneous recovery of a previously extinguished response

explanation: Bandura's Bobo doll work: children learned the behavior (acquisition) even without performing it; performance depended on incentives — the hallmark of latent observational learning.

stem: Fixed-ratio reinforcement schedules produce responses that are:

choices.text: Steady, with a brief pause after each reinforcement
Slow and constant regardless of reinforcement
Rapid and steady with no post-reinforcement pause
Unpredictable bursts tied to time intervals

explanation: Fixed-ratio schedules (reinforce every N responses) yield high response rates with a short pause after each reinforcer. Variable-ratio (C) produces high steady rates without the pause.

stem: After wearing a yellow-tinted ski mask for an hour, taking it off makes the snow look slightly bluish. This is best explained by:

choices.text: Sensory adaptation in opponent-process color channels
The volley principle in auditory processing
Weber's law applied to brightness differences

explanation: Prolonged yellow exposure fatigues yellow-processing cells; the opponent aftereffect biases perception toward blue — opponent-process theory.

stem: A child calls every four-legged animal "doggie." Later, she learns that only some are dogs. The refinement of her category is called:
explanation: Accommodation modifies an existing schema to fit new information; assimilation (B) would stretch the "doggie" schema to absorb cats without change.

stem: Which pair correctly matches a memory phenomenon with its stage of processing?

choices.text: Echoic memory — brief sensory store for auditory input

explanation: Echoic memory is the momentary (a few seconds) sensory register for sound. Chunking reorganizes encoding capacity (A); proactive interference is a retrieval phenomenon (C); spacing affects encoding (D).

stem: A woman attributes her poor exam grade to the test being unfairly difficult but attributes a friend's poor grade to laziness. This illustrates:

choices.text: The self-serving bias combined with the fundamental attribution error

explanation: Taking credit-protecting external excuses for oneself (self-serving bias) while explaining others' behavior dispositionally (fundamental attribution error).

stem: Research finds that as participants' groups grew larger, each individual was less likely to help a person in distress. This effect is best labeled:
explanation: Bystander effect: responsibility divides among onlookers as group size grows. Social loafing (A) concerns reduced effort on shared tasks, not helping decisions.

stem: Signal detection theory predicts that a radiologist expecting a high base rate of tumors will make more:
explanation: A liberal response criterion (biased toward saying "yes") raises hits at the cost of more false alarms — a core signal-detection tradeoff.

stem: Which scenario is the clearest example of negative reinforcement?

choices.text: A parent scolds a child for running into the street
Buckling your seatbelt stops the car's warning chime
A student loses screen time after skipping homework
A rat receives a food pellet for pressing a lever

explanation: Negative reinforcement removes an aversive stimulus (the chime) and increases the behavior (buckling). A and C add aversive outcomes (punishment); D is positive reinforcement.

stem: Design a study to test whether sleep affects memory consolidation in high school students.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: State a testable hypothesis for this study.
parts.referenceAnswer: Students who sleep 8 or more hours after learning a word list will recall more words 24 hours later than students who sleep 5 or fewer hours.
rubric: Hypothesis states a relationship between sleep and memory

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the independent and dependent variables and one variable that should be controlled.
parts.referenceAnswer: IV: hours of sleep (sleep condition). DV: number of words recalled after 24 hours. Controls: same word list, same learning time, same recall environment, similar baseline memory ability.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Explain how one ethical guideline applies to this study.
parts.referenceAnswer: Informed consent: student participants (and guardians if minors) must be told the purpose, procedures, and right to withdraw; the sleep restriction condition must be disclosed as a possible cost.
rubric: Applies it concretely to this study

stem: Use the source to answer the questions below.

materials.title: Study Vignette
materials.text: A researcher recruits 40 college students for a two-week study. Half are randomly assigned to use a mindfulness app for 10 minutes daily; half play a casual puzzle game. Before and after the two weeks, all participants complete a standardized anxiety questionnaire and keep a sleep diary. The mindfulness group reports lower anxiety scores and 25 more minutes of nightly sleep on average.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Identify the operational definition of the dependent variables in this study.
parts.referenceAnswer: Anxiety is operationalized as the score on the standardized anxiety questionnaire; sleep is operationalized as nightly sleep minutes from the diary.
rubric: Identifies questionnaire score as anxiety measure
Identifies diary minutes as sleep measure

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Name the design feature that supports a cause-and-effect claim and explain why it matters.
parts.referenceAnswer: Random assignment: it evenly distributes participant characteristics (baseline anxiety, sleep habits) across groups, so group differences at the end are attributable to the app rather than preexisting differences.
rubric: Explains control of confounds/enables causal inference

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Propose one change that would improve the study's validity.
parts.referenceAnswer: Add an active placebo condition matched for time and expectation, or blind the researchers scoring questionnaires, to reduce expectancy/demand effects.
rubric: Links it to a specific validity threat
